source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Apply suction while advancing the catheter and continue the suction application for about 30 seconds.","B":"Preoxygenate as indicated and limit each suction application to no more than about 15 seconds.","C":"Instill normal saline before every pass and use deep suction routinely for secretion removal.","D":"Perform suction on a fixed schedule even when assessment shows no clinical indication."}}
source_row.rationale: AARC recommends preoxygenation as indicated and limiting suction application to a maximum of 15 seconds. It generally advises against routine saline instillation, favors suctioning when indicated rather than on a fixed schedule, and reserves deep suctioning for cases in which shallow suction is ineffective. Option B is correct.
source_row.source_detail: Artificial Airway Suctioning guideline recommendations: suction only when indicated; preoxygenate adult/pediatric patients as appropriate; use sterile technique for open suctioning; generally avoid routine saline; limit suction application to a maximum of 15 seconds; use deep suction only if shallow suction is ineffective. 2022 AARC Artificial Airway Suctioning guideline remains an active evidence-based guideline on the AARC site; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, emergency response and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
